definitions.temporal_candidate: Public evidence supports a plausible earlier-to-later dependency and meaningful mishandling after an environmental, task, ownership, monitoring, or workflow transition. definitions.short_control: The observed or proposed defect is currently explained as a local operation, implementation, interpretation, or verification problem without an evidenced material historical dependency. It may be useful as a short baseline; it is not accepted as a long-running failure merely because the session or downstream job was long.
definitions.evidence_needed: A binding earlier obligation, agent attribution, actual failure/consequence, or the earlier-to-later chain is not sufficiently established to decide suitability. Collect the specified missing records before admission.

limits: This pass reads published submission metadata, prior case audits, and selected public evidence files; it does not open private raw histories or run new evaluations.
Short anchor distances do not disprove a broader historical mechanism, but no broader mechanism is assumed without evidence.
A historical error, a scripted checker pass, a fresh-agent error rate, and a controlled history effect are distinct claims.

Case source aliases and original anchor labels are preserved as reported; several are known to cover requests or recovery rather than the precise causal decision. They need refinement before controlled evaluation.
No candidate is described here as causally proven. Recovery and denied attempts must be distinguished from delivered damage in a later evaluator.

The 28 temporal candidates are mechanism candidates, not 28 established long-running failures. original_work_exposure describes independently whether substantive intervening agent work is actually exposed in the public record.
